headline: Maryland's three big utilities asked regulators to make data centers pay their own share of grid costs.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: the filing was made on 29 Sep 2026, four days before the window, and the Baltimore Sun text could not be read.
importance_line: More than a million Maryland households would be shielded from grid costs caused by data centers if the Public Service Commission accepts the proposal, but it is a filing, not a decision, with hearings running into December.
summary: Patch reports that BGE, Pepco and Delmarva Power filed a large-load tariff with the Maryland Public Service Commission on 29 Sep 2026, a rate plan that would require big new customers such as data centers to pay, in BGE's words, their "fair share toward the grid all customers rely on"; the Baltimore Sun followed on 2 Oct. The commission holds a first hearing on 23 Oct 2026, and the same utilities separately seek approval to return about $160 million in tax savings to customers after a July court ruling.
notes: Baltimore Sun (pool source) returned HTTP 200 with only a copyright notice, AMP too; Patch (30 Sep 2026) read instead and credited as its own report.
